stemMd: An exterior angle of a triangle is 137 degrees. One nonadjacent interior angle is 58 degrees. What is the other nonadjacent interior angle?
explanationMd: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two nonadjacent interior angles. Therefore the missing one is 137−58=79 degrees. The three interior angles 43,58,79 total 180.

distractorRationale.e: This adds the two given angles.
distractorRationale.d: This is the interior angle adjacent to the exterior angle.
distractorRationale.c: No equality of the two nonadjacent angles is specified.
distractorRationale.a: This subtracts 79 from 180, not the requested angle.
